Methodology: Partial Identification Under Differential Misclassification

Davood Tofighi, Ph.D.

2026-07-16

Source: vignettes/articles/methodology.qmd

Overview

medrobust provides bounds for natural direct and indirect effects (NDE/NIE) when the exposure or mediator is measured with differential misclassification — error whose sensitivity and specificity depend on the outcome YY. This vignette gives a self-contained method summary. For full derivations and convergence diagnostics, see the companion Identification Mathematics vignette.

Causal Framework

Consider binary exposure AA, binary mediator MM, binary outcome YY, and pre-exposure confounders CC. Under the standard potential-outcomes assumptions (no unmeasured confounding, consistency, positivity, cross-world independence), the natural effects compare counterfactual outcome means E[Y(a,M(a′))]E[Y(a, M(a'))]:

NDE:E[Y(1,M(0))]−E[Y(0,M(0))], \text{NDE}: \quad E[Y(1,M(0))] - E[Y(0,M(0))], NIE:E[Y(1,M(1))]−E[Y(1,M(0))]. \text{NIE}: \quad E[Y(1,M(1))] - E[Y(1,M(0))].

These are identified from the observed data via the g-formula:

E[Y(a,M(a′))]=∑cP(C=c)∑mP(M=m∣a′,c)P(Y=1∣a,m,c). E[Y(a, M(a'))] = \sum_c P(C{=}c) \sum_{m} P(M{=}m \mid a', c)\, P(Y{=}1 \mid a, m, c).

The key implementation point: the outcome expectation is taken after averaging over MM and CC, not by plugging in E[M]E[M]. Jensen-inequality bias would otherwise inflate the NDE and deflate the NIE.

Differential Misclassification Model

In practice, either the exposure or the mediator may be observed with error. medrobust handles two scenarios.

Mediator misclassification

The observed mediator M*M^* satisfies

Sny=P(M*=1∣M=1,Y=y),Spy=P(M*=0∣M=0,Y=y),y∈{0,1}. Sn_y = P(M^*{=}1 \mid M{=}1, Y{=}y), \qquad Sp_y = P(M^*{=}0 \mid M{=}0, Y{=}y), \qquad y \in \{0,1\}.

When Sn0=Sn1Sn_0 = Sn_1 and Sp0=Sp1Sp_0 = Sp_1 the error is non-differential and classical methods apply. medrobust targets the general case Sny≠Sn1−ySn_y \neq Sn_{1-y} or Spy≠Sp1−ySp_y \neq Sp_{1-y}, parameterized via odds ratios ψsn=(Sn1/Sn0)/((1−Sn1)/(1−Sn0))\psi_{sn} = (Sn_1/Sn_0)/((1-Sn_1)/(1-Sn_0)) and ψsp\psi_{sp} analogously.

Exposure misclassification

The observed exposure A*A^* satisfies the same structure with AA in place of MM. The four user-facing sensitivity parameters are the same: sn0,sp0,ψsn,ψspsn_0, sp_0, \psi_{sn}, \psi_{sp}.

Identification Strategy

Because sensitivity and specificity differ by outcome stratum, the observed joint distribution (in each (A,C)(A, C) or (M,C)(M, C) cell) decomposes into two independent 2×22 \times 2 linear systems — one for Y=1Y=1, one for Y=0Y=0. Each system is invertible if and only if

det⁡=Sny+Spy−1≠0. \det = Sn_y + Sp_y - 1 \neq 0.

Inverting these systems recovers the latent true probabilities P(M=m,Y=y∣a,c)P(M=m, Y=y \mid a, c) (mediator scenario) or P(A=a∣m,y,c)P(A=a \mid m, y, c) (exposure scenario), which are then passed to the g-formula to compute NDE and NIE. For the exposure path the inverse has a closed form (Cramér’s rule); for the mediator path the package solves the two 2×22 \times 2 systems per cell.

At the true sensitivity parameters, population recovery is exact to machine precision (<10−16<10^{-16}); at finite nn the bound converges to the truth as n→∞n \to \infty.

Testable Implications and Falsification

The model implies constraints on the observed data. For each misclassification parameter set Ψ=(sn0,sp0,ψsn,ψsp)\Psi = (sn_0, sp_0, \psi_{sn}, \psi_{sp}), medrobust checks whether the recovered latent probabilities are valid (all probabilities in [0,1][0,1], all conditional probabilities well-defined). Parameter sets that fail these checks are falsified — they are empirically incompatible with the data. The falsified region is a data-driven exclusion that typically shrinks the sensitivity space substantially.

check_compatibility() exposes this falsification test directly:

library(medrobust)
data("gesthtn")

compat <- check_compatibility(
  data = gesthtn,
  exposure = "A",
  mediator = "M_star",
  outcome = "Y",
  confounders = c("C1", "C2"),
  misclassified_variable = "mediator",
  sn0 = 0.90, sp0 = 0.85, psi_sn = 1.5, psi_sp = 1.2
)
print(compat)

Bounds Construction

For a sensitivity region — a user-specified hyper-rectangle [sn0min,sn0max]×[sp0min,sp0max]×[ψsnmin,ψsnmax]×[ψspmin,ψspmax][sn_0^{\min}, sn_0^{\max}] \times [sp_0^{\min}, sp_0^{\max}] \times [\psi_{sn}^{\min}, \psi_{sn}^{\max}] \times [\psi_{sp}^{\min}, \psi_{sp}^{\max}] — medrobust evaluates the effect at a grid of parameter sets (Latin Hypercube Sampling by default) and computes:

L̂=minΨ∈ℱeffect̂(Ψ),Û=maxΨ∈ℱeffect̂(Ψ), \hat L = \min_{\Psi \in \mathcal{F}} \widehat{\text{effect}}(\Psi), \qquad \hat U = \max_{\Psi \in \mathcal{F}} \widehat{\text{effect}}(\Psi),

where ℱ\mathcal{F} is the non-falsified subset of the grid. The resulting interval [L̂,Û][\hat L, \hat U] is the partial-identification bound.

Confidence Intervals

The estimated bound [L̂,Û][\hat L, \hat U] is consistent but is not a confidence set for the true effect: when the identified interval is narrow relative to endpoint sampling uncertainty, naive coverage is well below the nominal level. The Imbens–Manski (2004) construction corrects this by widening each endpoint by its standard error:

[L̂−cSÊ(L̂),Û+cSÊ(Û)], \bigl[\hat L - c\,\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}(\hat L),\; \hat U + c\,\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}(\hat U)\bigr],

where cc interpolates between the one-sided and two-sided critical values. bound_ci() implements this; the endpoint SEs are obtained by re-evaluating the effect at the fixed optimal Ψ\Psi on bootstrap resamples (no full grid search per resample). Empirically this restores approximately nominal coverage across both misclassification paths, multiple nn, and multiple effect scales (OR, RR, RD).

bounds <- bound_ne(
  data = gesthtn,
  exposure = "A",
  mediator = "M_star",
  outcome = "Y",
  confounders = c("C1", "C2"),
  misclassified_variable = "mediator",
  sensitivity_region = sensitivity_region(
    sn0_range = c(0.80, 0.95),
    sp0_range = c(0.80, 0.95),
    psi_sn_range = c(1.0, 2.0),
    psi_sp_range = c(1.0, 2.0)
  ),
  n_grid = 50
)

ci <- bound_ci(
  bounds,
  data = gesthtn,
  exposure = "A",
  mediator = "M_star",
  outcome = "Y",
  confounders = c("C1", "C2"),
  misclassified_variable = "mediator",
  n_boot = 500L,
  level = 0.95
)
print(ci)

Assumptions and Scope

medrobust makes the following assumptions:

  • No unmeasured confounding between (A,M,Y)(A, M, Y) after conditioning on CC.
  • Consistency and positivity in the usual potential-outcomes sense.
  • Cross-world independence: M(a′)⟂Y(a,m)∣CM(a') \perp Y(a, m) \mid C (required for NDE/NIE identification even without measurement error).
  • The misclassification model is correctly specified: error depends only on YY (differential), not on other unmeasured variables.
  • The sensitivity parameters lie in the user-supplied region. The bounds are valid for every Ψ\Psi in that region simultaneously; if the true Ψ\Psi lies outside the region, the bounds may not contain the truth.

References

  • Tofighi, D. (2025). Partial identification of causal mediation effects under differential misclassification. Manuscript in preparation.
  • Imbens, G. W., & Manski, C. F. (2004). Confidence intervals for partially identified parameters. Econometrica, 72(6), 1845–1857.
  • Manski, C. F. (2003). Partial Identification of Probability Distributions. Springer.
  • VanderWeele, T. J. (2015). Explanation in Causal Inference. Oxford University Press.
